summary.text: Ammonites are extinct cephalopods with typically coiled shells, more closely related to octopuses and squid than to the nautiluses they resemble.
They appeared around 410 million years ago, and the last ones vanished during or soon after the extinction event about 66 million years ago.
Their fossils are excellent index fossils, used to tie the rock layers holding a given species to specific periods of geologic time.

items.prompt: A geologist finds the same ammonite species in rock layers at two sites far apart in one country. What does this most reasonably tell her?

options.label: Both layers are the same type of rock
Both layers formed at the same water depth
Both layers date from the same span of time
Both sites were once part of one beach

items.explain: Ammonites are index fossils: finding a particular species links a rock layer to a specific geologic time period.

items.prompt: An ammonite shell is split into many chambers by thin walls. Where in the shell did the living animal sit?

options.label: Only in the last and largest chamber
Stretched through the whole coiled shell
In the small chamber at the very center
Outside, clinging to the shell's surface

items.explain: The animal occupied only the body chamber, the last and largest one, adding bigger chambers at the open end as it grew.

items.prompt: Ammonite shells look a lot like nautilus shells. Which living animals are ammonites actually closer kin to?

options.label: Nautiluses
Snails and slugs
Crabs and lobsters
Octopuses and squid

items.explain: Despite the look-alike shells, ammonoids are more closely related to octopuses, squid and cuttlefish than to nautiluses.

items.prompt: The name "ammonite" traces back to the Egyptian god Ammon. What links the fossils to him?

options.label: His temples were built of fossil stone
He was shown wearing coiled rams' horns
His priests carried the shells as charms
He was said to rule over the seas

items.explain: The spiral shells resemble tightly coiled rams' horns, and Ammon was usually shown wearing rams' horns, so Pliny called them horns of Ammon.

items.prompt: After the Chicxulub impact, nautiluses survived but ammonites died out. What is one suggested reason?

options.label: Their tiny drifting young were hit by ocean acidification
Their heavy shells kept them from rising to the surface
Their eyes could not find food in the darkened seas
Their shells dissolved while they rested on the sea floor

items.explain: Ammonite larvae were likely small and planktonic, so impact-driven ocean acidification would have hit them hard, while nautiluses laid eggs on the sea floor away from such effects.

items.prompt: How wide could the shell of one of the largest-known ammonites grow?

options.label: About 5 cm
About 25 cm
About 2 m
About 10 cm

items.explain: Parapuzosia seppenradensis, one of the largest-known ammonites, sometimes reached 2 m in diameter.
